channel.title: Conversion in Halacha — Dayan Daniel Kada
channel.description: Dayan Daniel Kada's classes on conversion: the Montefiore semikhah course (2021) on kabbalat misvot, the Beit Din and converting children, and a 2022 Tuesday-night shiur on Ruth and Orpah.
channel.itunes:author: Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: Does a Convert Need to Know Every Misvah? | Conversion in Halacha | Siman 268
item.description:
After milah and tevilah comes kabbalat misvot, and the sources seem to pull in two directions. The class sets the Gemara in Bekhorot against the Beit Yosef, the Darkei Moshe, the Rambam and the two statements in Shulhan Arukh Yoreh Deah 268.

item.title: Who Can Sit on a Conversion Beit Din? | Conversion in Halacha | Siman 268
item.description:
How many judges does each stage of conversion need, and what standing must they have? The Gemara in Yevamot and Tosafot on three for kabbalat misvot, how this applies to Reform and Conservative conversions that a Beit Din meets in ketubot and gittin, and how a woman immerses.

item.title: Does a Fetus Convert With Its Mother? | Conversion in Halacha | Siman 268
item.description:
Converting a civil couple lishem ishut (Rashi, Ramban, the Rambam's sauce and the Ahiezer), and a woman who immerses while pregnant: is the fetus an extension of its mother or an independent convert, and what that changes for the Beit Din's knowledge, the child's right to object, and milah on Shabbat.

item.title: Can a Beit Din Convert a Child? | Conversion in Halacha | Siman 268
item.description:
Can a child become Jewish without choosing it? The Gemara in Ketubot and Siman 268: a minor is converted on the authority of the Beit Din because conversion is a benefit, how zakhin works for a child, and the Rashba and Tosafot on the difficulties.

item.title: What If You Only Learn at 25 That You Were Converted? | Conversion in Halacha | Siman 268
item.description:
When a convert child may object after bar or bat misvah and why the objection works retroactively, the Hatam Sofer's problem and Rav Moshe's rule that children must be told before marriage, then whether a convert may hold positions of authority (dayan, Rosh Yeshiva, rabbi, mashgiach) and Rav Uziel's encouraging approach.
